question: Why can telling a person with insomnia to try to stay awake help them fall asleep?
answer: Because the effort to sleep is part of what keeps them awake. Sleep comes when arousal drops, and straining for it raises arousal: clock-watching, counting hours left, willing the body off. Told to lie in the dark and keep their eyes open, many relax the effort and drift off. Chasing sleep scares it away.
move: Some states arrive only when you stop trying to produce them.
reference: Morgenthaler, Kramer, Alessi et al., Practice parameters for the psychological and behavioral treatment of insomnia: an update, Sleep, 2006
